catalog_entry.mechanism: All three events are exhibitions generated by who participates and how they are used, not by season-long roles. In the All-Star Game, selection and withdrawal define the pool, managers rotate starters, reserves and one-inning pitchers, and a tie after nine innings goes to a swing-off whose statistics do not count for player props; the MVP is a panel and fan choice. The Futures Game is a seven-inning prospect exhibition priced from translated minor-league talent. In the 2026 Derby, an eight-player field takes 20 swings in a Round 1 pool and 15 in the semifinal and final, so homers are per-swing HR rate times a fixed allotment plus last-swing extensions, and longest-homer, 500+ ft and exit-velocity series are tail extremes over a draw count set by rounds reached.

interactions.hypothesis: A hitter's expected ASG homers equal his chance of appearing times his expected PA times a small per-PA HR rate, so a power hitter on the bench contributes little while a starter contributes by a PA count that a regular-season lineup slot would overstate.

With swings fixed per round, a hittable and repeatable batting-practice pitcher raises HR per swing multiplicatively with the hitter's power, and the last-swing extension makes the gain convex for high-rate hitters.

Tailwind, thin air or a short sector shift the distance distribution by a few feet; for a 500 ft threshold in the far upper tail this small shift changes exceedance probability by a large relative amount.

Player HR props ignore swing-off homers, but the combined game-HR total is silent, so the total-HR distribution is a mixture over tie and no-tie regimes whose right tail depends on how the swing-off is counted.
MVP credit goes almost only to the winning side, so a player's MVP probability is his share of winning-side key events times the winner probability, with a star-name tilt in close calls.

contract.settlement_definition: All 20 live series now have sampled rules text (2026 events). All-Star Game: KXMLBASGAME pays Yes if the National League wins the game 'originally scheduled for Jul 14, 2026'; a postponement within two days keeps the market open, longer or cancellation resolves at a fair price; a swing-off decides the winner. Named-player props KXMLBASGHIT (1+ hit), KXMLBASGHR (1+ HR) and KXMLBASGKS (2+ strikeouts) are per-player, resolve No if the player does not enter, and for hits/HR exclude swing-off statistics. KXMLBALLSTARHR counts home runs by all players combined (7+) with no swing-off clause. KXMLBASGMVP settles on the official MVP award. KXMLBFTGAME pays on the National League winning the Futures Game, with the same two-day postponement rule. Home Run Derby: winner, finals qualifier, Round 2 qualifier, Round 1 leader, longest HR and highest exit velocity resolve No if the player does not participate, with dead-heat 1/N on ties; the final matchup and forecast need both named players in the final; the Round 2 over/under counts the player's Round 2 homers (7+); KXMLBHRDERBYQUAL resolves Yes on selection even if the player then does not participate; event totals are HR count (140+), 500+ ft HR count (6+) and any HR of 525+ ft. Distance and exit velocity ties are judged 'according to the Governing League'.

variants_and_edge_cases: Player props KXMLBASGHIT/KXMLBASGHR exclude swing-off statistics; KXMLBALLSTARHR (combined game HR) has no such clause, so whether swing-off homers count toward the total is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

Non-appearance is No (not void) for all ASG player props and for Derby participant markets, so participation probability multiplies the price; KXMLBHRDERBYQUAL is the exception and resolves Yes on selection.
KXMLBHRDERBYOU counts Round 2 homers only; a player eliminated in Round 1 has zero Round 2 homers and the text implies No, though it is not stated explicitly.
KXMLBHRDERBYR1LEAD and KXMLBHRDERBYSEMI dead-heat ties at 1/N, while the 2026 Derby itself breaks Round 1 ties by longest home run, so the market and the league can disagree on a tie.

2026 Derby format (press reports, June 2026): 20 swings in Round 1 pool play (top four advance), 15 swings in the semifinal and final, a homer on the last swing extends the round, semifinal/final ties go to a three-swing swing-off; whether swing-off and extension homers count toward event totals, 500+ ft counts and longest HR is not stated.
KXMLBASGAME and KXMLBFTGAME survive a postponement of up to two days; beyond that they resolve to a fair price, not void.
KXMLBASGMVP settles on the official award, which is chosen by a panel with a fan ballot component whose weight is not stated in the rules.

mechanism.summary: All-Star Week outcomes come from three exhibition processes with no standings stakes. In the All-Star Game, a pool of selected players is cut by acceptance and withdrawal, the managers rotate starters, reserves and one-inning pitchers, and a nine-inning tie goes to a swing-off whose statistics do not count for player props; a handful of plate appearances then produces hits, homers and strikeouts as rare-event counts, a non-appearance settles player props No, and the MVP is a panel-plus-fan judgement of winning-side events. The Futures Game is a seven-inning prospect game with its own talent scale. In the 2026 Derby, eight hitters take 20 swings in a Round 1 pool (top four advance) and 15 swings in the semifinal and final, so homers are a fixed allotment times per-swing HR rate (driven by power, selectivity and the chosen pitcher) plus last-swing extensions; distance and exit-velocity markets are extremes over homers whose number depends on rounds reached. Participation, not talent, is the dominant uncertainty for player markets.

stages.name: Selection, acceptance and withdrawal
stages.description: Rosters come from fan vote phases, player ballots and commissioner fill; Derby participants come from invitations that stars often decline. Between announcement and event, injuries and personal choices remove players and replacements enter. KXMLBHRDERBYQUAL settles on selection alone (Yes even if the player later withdraws), while every ASG player prop and every other Derby market resolves No for a non-participant, so this stage multiplies straight into those prices.
stages.distribution: Binary membership per player with correlated late changes; withdrawal hazard rises near the event date.

stages.name: Exhibition usage plan
stages.description: Two managers fill a card with starters, then rotate reserves; pitchers each throw about one inning in a planned order. This determines PA per hitter (zero to about three) and batters faced per arm, and so the chance that a named player enters at all, which the rules treat as No when he does not. Since 2022 (rule in place from the 2022 CBA, first used in 2025) a nine-inning tie is settled by a swing-off rather than extra innings, so regulation exposure is capped at nine innings.
stages.distribution: Discrete PA counts with many zeros and ones; pitcher batters faced concentrated at 3-5; regime shifts by year.

stages.name: Per-PA outcomes in the exhibition
stages.description: Given a PA, the hit, HR or strikeout chance depends on the hitter's contact and power profile and the arm's whiff and HR vulnerability, with hitters swinging freely and pitchers throwing at maximum effort for one inning. Host park and weather shift HR probability multiplicatively. Because PA counts are tiny, outcomes are rare-event Bernoulli draws with large relative variance.
stages.distribution: Low-count Bernoulli/Poisson-binomial; HR rate small per PA, so zero-inflated totals.

stages.name: Team score, winner and shared-day dispersion
stages.description: Runs and HR aggregate over both teams' exposures; a common day-level factor (wind, ball, pitcher usage) correlates HR counts across the game. The winner follows from nine-inning runs or, if tied, the swing-off. The combined game-HR rung (7+) is silent on swing-off homers, unlike the player props, so its tail depends on a counting rule the text does not give.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed team and HR totals; winner near coin-flip with league talent a mild tilt; MVP heavy-tailed credit.

stages.name: Derby rounds under the swing-capped format
stages.description: Round 1 is an eight-man pool of 20 swings each; the top four by homers advance, Round 1 ties broken by longest homer. Semifinal and final are head-to-head rounds of 15 swings, ties settled by three-swing swing-offs. A homer on the last allotted swing extends the round until a non-homer. Per-swing HR rate (power, selectivity, chosen pitcher, park) times the allotment sets round totals; Round 1 leader, Round 2 qualifier, Round 2 over/under, finalist, final matchup, forecast and winner markets all settle on this stage.
stages.distribution: Binomial count per round with a geometric last-swing extension tail; positive within-hitter correlation across rounds; advancement is an order statistic over the pool.

stages.name: Derby extremes: distance and exit velocity
stages.description: Longest homer, 500+ ft count, the 525 ft longest-distance threshold and highest exit velocity are order statistics over all Derby homers. They depend on each hitter's tail, on air carry at the host park and on how many homers he hits, which under fixed swings is set by rounds reached. They correlate with s5 through advancement and through the Round 1 longest-homer tiebreak, and ties are dead-heated at league-reported precision.
stages.distribution: Generalized Pareto/Gumbel-type tails; discrete 500+ counts; ties possible at reported precision.

stages.name: All-Star Game MVP selection
stages.description: After the game a panel with a fan ballot names the MVP. The choice concentrates on the winning league's player with the most visible contribution (go-ahead homer, multi-hit game, decisive swing-off moment), with a tilt toward star names in close calls. The MVP series therefore depends on winner probability, on each player's chance of producing a key event in his few plate appearances, and on voter bias.
stages.distribution: Categorical over roughly 60 players with heavy concentration on winning-side hitters with an HR or go-ahead hit; small residual mass on pitchers.

stages.name: Futures Game prospect exhibition
stages.description: The Futures Game is a seven-inning NL vs AL game of minor-league prospects played two days before the All-Star Game, with short pitcher stints and wide talent variation across levels. Strength comes from translated minor-league performance and prospect grades rather than major-league ratings; postponement within two days keeps the market open, otherwise it settles at a fair price.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli winner near 0.5 with a small talent tilt; high variance from seven innings and rotating arms.

mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.label: All-Star Game roster, starters and planned participation (who plays, in which slot, for how many innings)
mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.mechanism: Each hitter's plate appearances and each pitcher's batters faced in the exhibition are set by roster composition, the two managers' substitution habits and the announced pitching order, not by a season-long role.
mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.rationale: A player who is named but enters in the 6th inning gets one or two PAs; a starter gets two or three. Pitchers are normally used for one inning each, so strikeouts come from many arms facing a few batters. Withdrawn players are replaced by commissioner picks, which changes both pool and slots. Every per-player ASG market is first a participation question.
mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.measurement: Per ASG year 2012-2025 build a table of plate appearances by lineup slot (starter vs reserve entry inning) and batters faced by pitcher role (starter, middle, closer-type). Estimate P(plays at all | selected, position, reserve status) and E[PA | plays] by league/manager, shrunk to the 14-year pooled mean with k = 3 games. For the target year use the posted rosters, listed starters and probable pitchers as of the market timestamp; refresh at lineup announcement (about 1-2 hours before first pitch). Output per player: P(any PA), PA distribution over {0,1,2,3,4}; per pitcher: P(pitches), expected BF.

mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.why: Hits, HR and strikeout contracts and the MVP are conditional on appearing; participation is the dominant source of variance and zeros in this event.

mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.label: All-Star Game format and tiebreak regime for the year (innings, extra-inning or swing-off rule, pitcher limits)
mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.mechanism: The rulebook for the year decides how long the exhibition lasts if tied and whether the tiebreak produces countable events.
mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.rationale: Since 2022 (first actually used in 2025) a game tied after nine innings goes to a swing-off (three hitters per side) instead of extra innings, and earlier years used automatic-runner extras; the 2026 rules text confirms a swing-off can end the game. Player hit and HR props exclude swing-off statistics, but the combined game-HR total does not say so, so the regime changes both the winner distribution and which events can count.
mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.measurement: Per ASG year 2000-2026 store scheduled innings, extra-inning rule (traditional, automatic runner, or swing-off after 9), pitcher limits, DH use, roster size, whether swing-off events count in game and player statistics, and the official announcement date from MLB press releases. P(tied after 9 innings) = games tied after nine / games played over 2010-2025 (2020 excluded, no game), with a Beta(1, 9) prior. Historical games get weight 1.0 if the extra-inning rule matches the current year and 0.4 otherwise. Any rule announced after the market snapshot is excluded from features and flagged. Output: regime flags, P(tie after 9), and the counting rule for swing-off events.

mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.why: Fixes the event window for hits/HR/strikeout totals and decides what a tie means for the winner market.

mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.label: Home Run Derby field: who is invited, who accepts, withdrawal and replacement hazard, seeding
mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.mechanism: The Derby field is a self-selected set of hitters, so qualifier and winner markets depend on acceptance, injury withdrawals and replacement choices.
mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.rationale: Top sluggers often decline, and replacements arrive days before the event (Murakami was the eighth and final addition in 2026 after returning from the injured list). The field is both an input and a target: KXMLBHRDERBYQUAL settles Yes on selection even if the player then withdraws, while every other Derby market resolves No for a non-participant. Round 1 in 2026 is pool play, so seeding no longer sets Round 1 opponents; semifinal pairings follow Round 1 rank.
mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.measurement: For each year 2015-2025 record the invited list at announcement dates, acceptance, final eight, replacements and seeding rule. Model P(accept | rank in season HR, prior participation, age, team home park hosting, injury status) as a logistic with shrinkage k = 5 per feature group. As-of: use announcements dated before the market snapshot; late replacement flagged separately. Output: P(player in final eight) and the seed table.
raw_data: derby participants with announcement dates, replacements, seeding by year
season HR to date at announcement
mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.why: Qualifier, finalist and matchup markets cannot be priced without a probability distribution over who is actually in the bracket.

mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.label: Home Run Derby round output under the 2026 swing-capped format: swings allotted, per-swing HR rate, last-swing extension and advancement
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.mechanism: With a fixed swing allotment (20 in Round 1, 15 in the semifinal and final) a round's homers equal the sum of per-swing HR indicators plus a geometric extension when the last allotted swing is a homer; the clock, pitcher pace and bonus time no longer exist.
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.rationale: Under swing caps volume is fixed, so the levers are per-swing HR rate, selectivity (takes appear not to count against the allotment, so waiting for a hittable pitch costs nothing but time) and the quality of the hitter's chosen batting-practice pitcher. Round 1 is an eight-man pool where the top four advance, so the advancement threshold depends on the whole field's rates, not on one opponent.
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.measurement: Per hitter: p = P(HR | swing) estimated from season barrel rate, pulled fly-ball rate and max-EV percentile (through the day before the Derby) mapped to Derby HR per swing using 2015-2025 Derby swing logs (timed-format years, swing outcomes only, not volume), shrunk to the pooled Derby mean with k = 40 swings, adjusted by the BP-pitcher term and host-park carry. Round HR ~ Binomial(n_r, p) + extension E where E is geometric with P(last swing HR) x p/(1-p) expected extra homers; n_r = 20, 15, 15. Fatigue as a multiplicative decay on p per round (prior 0.97, shrunk). Simulate the pool, the longest-HR Round 1 tiebreak and three-swing swing-offs. As-of: field and rulebook at the snapshot.

mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.label: Derby extremes: probability of 500+ foot homers, longest homer and peak exit velocity over the event
mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.mechanism: Longest-HR, 500+ ft count and highest exit velocity are maxima of batted-ball distributions over a few hundred swings, so they live in the upper tail of each hitter's power distribution.
mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.rationale: A batter's average HR distance says little about whether he reaches 500 or 525 ft. Tail behaviour needs top-decile EV and distance, park and wind carry, and the number of homers he gets, which under the 2026 format is set by rounds reached. Longest and highest-EV series are dead-heated at the league's reported precision, so rounding matters.
mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.measurement: For each hitter fit a generalized Pareto tail to HR distances and exit velocities above his own 85th percentile over 3 seasons of Statcast (min 25 exceedances, else borrow league shape and use own scale shrunk with k = 15), plus a Derby uplift estimated from 2015-2025 Derby versus in-game tails. Number of draws per hitter = homers from the throughput model, i.e. 20 Round 1 swings, plus 15 more if he reaches the semifinal and 15 more in the final, plus extensions; this makes extremes depend on bracket advancement, not clock. Adjust for host-park carry from mlb.park_specific_xhr and weather. Simulate jointly with the throughput model because the Round 1 tie rule (longest HR) couples totals and distances; report P(any >= 525 ft), P(500+ count >= k), P(each hitter has longest), P(each hitter has highest EV HR). As-of: games through the previous day.

mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.why: These contracts settle on one extreme value, where mean power and tail power are different things.

mlb.hr_derby_bp_pitcher_pairing.label: Home Run Derby batting-practice pitcher chosen by each hitter: identity, pitch speed and location consistency, past Derby results
mlb.hr_derby_bp_pitcher_pairing.mechanism: Per-swing HR rate depends on how hittable and repeatable the batting-practice pitches are; each hitter picks his own pitcher (often a coach or relative), so the pitcher is a hitter-specific matchup input.
mlb.hr_derby_bp_pitcher_pairing.rationale: With swings fixed, a pitcher who puts the ball in the hitter's preferred zone at a steady speed raises HR per swing directly, and an erratic one forces takes and weak swings. Pitcher history across hitters (the same coach pitching several Derbies) gives a partial pooling base.
mlb.hr_derby_bp_pitcher_pairing.measurement: Record pitcher identity per participant from announcements. Where Statcast Derby pitch tracking exists: mean and SD of release speed and plate location distance from the hitter's preferred zone per pitch, 2015-2025. Pitcher effect = random effect on logit P(HR | swing) in a hitter + pitcher model fitted on Derby swing logs, shrunk to 0 with k = 60 swings; unknown pitchers get the pooled mean. As-of: pitcher announcement before the snapshot.

mlb.asg_mvp_vote_model.label: All-Star Game MVP selection: panel plus fan ballot credit model over game performance, team result and star profile
mlb.asg_mvp_vote_model.mechanism: The MVP is chosen after the game by a selection panel with a fan ballot component, so it rewards a decisive hit or homer for the winning league, weighted by name recognition.
mlb.asg_mvp_vote_model.rationale: The award almost always goes to a player on the winning side with the game's most visible contribution (go-ahead homer, multi-hit game); fan voting adds a star-name bias for close calls. A swing-off decision changes credit because swing-off events are visible but may not count as game statistics.
mlb.asg_mvp_vote_model.measurement: From ASG box scores 2000-2025 build per-player credit features: winning-side flag, HR, RBI, go-ahead or tying event flag, hits, strikeouts for pitchers, inning of key event, and a star index (career All-Star selections, social follower rank). Fit a conditional logit for P(MVP | game events) and integrate over simulated game outcomes from the participation and per-PA models. Panel and fan weights taken from the year's MLB announcement (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED until checked). As-of: rosters and lineups at the snapshot.

mlb.futures_game_prospect_strength.label: Futures Game roster strength: prospect hitting and pitching quality by league from minor-league stats translated to a common scale
mlb.futures_game_prospect_strength.mechanism: The Futures Game is a seven-inning NL vs AL exhibition of prospects with short pitcher stints, so the winner depends on translated minor-league talent of the two rosters and on how many innings each arm covers.
mlb.futures_game_prospect_strength.rationale: Talent is minor-league and heterogeneous (Double-A teenagers next to Triple-A arms), so major-league ratings do not exist; translated stats and prospect grades are the only strength measure. The game is short, so variance is high and the talent edge is small.
mlb.futures_game_prospect_strength.measurement: Estimate level translation factors for A, High-A, Double-A and Triple-A from 2015-2025 players seen at a level and then in MLB the next season: factor_L = PA-weighted MLB wRC+ (FIP for pitchers) / prior-season level wRC+ (FIP), with an age adjustment for age relative to level median. Translated stat for each rostered prospect = current-season minor-league wRC+ or FIP times factor_L, blended 70/30 with the prospect-list grade mapped to wRC+/FIP by the same historical mapping, shrunk to the level mean with k = 150 PA or 40 IP. Team strength = PA-weighted lineup score (planned PA by slot from 2023-2025 seven-inning box scores) and innings-weighted pitching score. As-of: roster announcements and replacements before the snapshot.

interactions.mechanism: A hitter's expected ASG homers equal his chance of appearing times his expected PA times a small per-PA HR rate, so a power hitter on the bench contributes little while a starter contributes by a PA count that a regular-season lineup slot would overstate.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress ASG HR on predicted P(any PA) x E[PA] x season HR rate versus season HR rate alone across 2012-2025 starters and reserves.

interactions.mechanism: Under a fixed swing allotment the chosen pitcher's speed and location consistency scale the hitter's per-swing HR probability; the gain compounds through the last-swing extension, so a good pairing helps high-rate hitters more than low-rate ones.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit logit P(HR | swing) on Derby swing logs with hitter and pitcher random effects and their product; check whether pitcher effects are larger for hitters above the median HR rate.

interactions.mechanism: Tailwind, thin air or a short sector shift the distance distribution by a few feet; for a 500 ft threshold in the far upper tail this small shift changes exceedance probability by a large relative amount.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit exceedance counts of 480+ ft in derbies by host-park carry factor and compare slope against median distance slope.

interactions.mechanism: Player HR props exclude swing-off homers by rule, but the combined game-HR rung does not say so; if swing-off homers count, a tied game adds a block of near-certain homers and gives the total a right tail, otherwise only nine innings matter.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the 7+ total under both counting rules using P(tie after nine) from 2012-2025 scores and compare the probability gap with the strike ladder.

interactions.mechanism: Derby acceptance is correlated with All-Star selection, injury and hosting; a top slugger's refusal moves the replacement's expected power and the whole bracket jointly, not one participant at a time.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate field replacement sequences and test whether a joint acceptance model beats independent acceptance on historical Derby fields.

interactions.mechanism: With the roof closed wind has no effect, with it open wind component along the pull side changes carry; the host park decides which regime is active.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact wind component with a roof-open indicator on historical Derby distances and ASG HR at retractable-roof hosts.

interactions.mechanism: Rounds reached set how many homers a hitter contributes to the longest, 500+ ft and highest-EV draws, and the Round 1 tie rule rewards a long homer, so advancement and distance extremes are positively dependent and cannot be priced separately.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the event jointly versus with independent extreme draws and compare predicted longest-HR winner shares against 2015-2026 Derby outcomes.

interactions.mechanism: MVP probability is concentrated on the winning league, so a player's MVP chance is roughly winner probability times his share of winning-side key events; when the winner is a near coin flip, star-name bias in the fan ballot decides more close calls.
interactions.how_to_test: Across 2000-2025 ASGs regress MVP choice on winning-side flag, key-event WPA and a star index, and test whether the star term rises when WPA leaders are close.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in per-swing HR rate: fixed-allotment mean plus a geometric last-swing extension p^2/(1-p)
nonlinearities.why: With n fixed swings the expected round total is about n*p plus an extension term that grows like p^2/(1-p), so high-rate hitters gain disproportionately and round totals have a right tail.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy-tailed (generalized Pareto) response above the hitter's 85th percentile
nonlinearities.why: Extreme markets resolve on the single largest distance or EV, so the mean has little information and the tail shape controls the probability.

nonlinearities.shape: step function: PA in {0,1,2,3} with a point mass at 0 that maps to No
nonlinearities.why: Rotating substitution makes PA small integers, and the rules settle non-appearance as No, so player-prop prices are zero-inflated and jump with starter versus reserve status.

catalog_entry.label: Labour stoppage and league season-schedule markets
contract_types: Regular-season games played above a threshold
catalog_entry.target: Whether the MLB regular season starts before a date or plays more than N games, as determined by collective bargaining, any lockout or strike, and the games the league cancels.
catalog_entry.mechanism: The outcome is produced by owner-union collective bargaining after the CBA expires on December 1, 2026, not by games. Agreement before or after expiry, an owners' lockout decision, deadline hazards (spring training, scheduled opener) and the ramp-up after a deal set the first game date. More than 600 of 2,430 games fails only if no season is staged or play starts around mid-August, so that contract turns on a late go/no-go decision about a truncated season (2020 versus 1994-95) and on the non-agreement route of impasse, replacement players or an NLRB injunction.

inputs.why: Gap between owner and union stated positions governs the chance a deal is reached before games are lost.
Calendar of expiry, report and scheduled opening dates turns bargaining state into dated hazards.
Few comparable stoppages exist, so a reference class gives the prior for stoppage length.
Estimated revenue and pay at risk for each side determine who concedes; revenue splits are third-party estimates.
Maps start date to games playable; locates the late-start cutoff for 600 games, where compression no longer matters.
CBA expiry date, lockout flag, expected end and transaction freeze rules define the regime.
Scenario table of lockout probability, start and end dates, and games lost under each case.
Reports of talks, offers and deadlines arrive before official statements.
Source reliability weights leaks about proposals and sessions when sources conflict.
Official-game and suspended-game rules decide how partially played games count toward games played.
Service-time and roster-freeze rules show what changes during a lockout; indirect effect on bargaining topics.
Transaction timeline shows whether a freeze is on; informative about lockout state only.
Payroll and tax position indicates owner demands on cost control.
Free-agent class and arbitration status signal how many players feel urgent pressure.
Exact wording of the first-game and games-played conditions fixes what counts.
Market lifecycle events (halts, rule edits) identify when contract text changes.
Whether a minimum truncated season is staged or the year is cancelled decides the 600-game contract.
Impasse, replacement players and an NLRB injunction are a non-agreement route to games being played.

interactions.hypothesis: The hazard of agreement in a given week is a baseline deadline hazard scaled by the gap size; the same deadline closes a small gap with high probability and a structural gap (such as a cap demand) with low probability, so the effect of a deadline depends on how wide the gap is.

Once the remaining calendar falls below a minimum viable season, staging depends on whether postseason media revenue is at risk for owners and pay is pro-rated for players; the same calendar date gives opposite outcomes under different leverage.

The reference class is informative only if the leverage regime resembles the historical episode; when television revenue is guaranteed (owners' cost of waiting lower) long stoppages are more likely than the baseball sample implies.

Once a lockout is declared the process moves from a pre-expiry regime where deals are common near the deadline to a lockout regime where only paycheck pressure and calendar deadlines close the gap, so new reports have different weights in each regime.

contract.settlement_definition: KXMLBOPENINGDAY settles Yes if the first game of the 2027 MLB regular season has taken place before May 31, 2027. KXMLBSEASONGAMES settles Yes if the number of MLB regular-season games played in 2027 is above 600 (strike type greater, floor 600), read as league games of 2,430 scheduled, though team-games are not excluded by the text. The rules do not define whether suspended or shortened games count, whether games staged with replacement players count as 'MLB regular season games', the time zone of the date boundary, or a data source, so verification is partial.

rules_evidence.quote: If the first game in the 2027 MLB regular season has taken place prior to May 31, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Condition is the date of the first regular-season game, not the scheduled date; a lockout delaying the opener past May 30 resolves No.

rules_evidence.quote: If the number of MLB regular season games played is above 600 games in the 2027 MLB regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Strict greater-than threshold on total games played league-wide; far below 2,430 scheduled games, so only a near-cancelled season resolves No.

variants_and_edge_cases: The opener series settles on when the first game occurred, not when it was scheduled; if a lockout moves the opening to May 30 versus May 31 the date boundary matters and time zone is not stated.
Strike type greater means exactly 600 games resolves No; one rung is sampled and other thresholds may exist for the same series.

Count unit: 'number of MLB regular season games played' is most naturally league games (2,430 scheduled), but team-games (4,860) are not excluded; 600 is about 40 games per team on the league-game reading.
Suspended or shortened games are not addressed. Tiebreaker games (Game 163) were abolished from 2022 and matter only if a new CBA reinstates them.
An international opening series (MLB opened 2025 in Tokyo in mid-March) would be the 'first game' for KXMLBOPENINGDAY; relevant only if a deal lands close to the scheduled opener.
Games staged with replacement players after an owners' impasse declaration (1995 spring precedent) would plausibly be 'MLB regular season games' for both contracts; the text does not say.

A season that begins on time but later suffers a mid-season strike would affect the games-played contract but not the Opening Day contract; once 601 games are played the games contract is settled Yes.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules. Presumed: official MLB schedule results and the league's game log (MLB Stats API).

mechanism.summary: Neither contract is decided on the field. The outcome is a bargaining process between ownership and the players' union after the collective agreement expires on December 1, 2026: whether a deal precedes expiry, whether owners lock out, how long agreement takes at the deadlines (spring-training reporting, scheduled opener), and the ramp-up needed before games. Opening Day before May 31 requires agreement, or an injunction or imposed terms, plus a ramp-up before that date. More than 600 of 2,430 games fails only if no season is staged or play starts around mid-August, so that contract is a deep-tail question decided by a late go/no-go on a truncated season (2020 staged 60 games; 1994-95 cancelled) and by the impasse, replacement-player and labour-board route, not by make-up scheduling.

stages.name: Bargaining state before and after CBA expiry
stages.description: The agreement expires on December 1, 2026. Before then the owners decide whether to bargain to a deal, accept an extension or prepare a lockout; the union decides whether to authorize a strike. Positions on economic structure (cap, floor, revenue sharing, tax, pre-arbitration pay) set whether a gap exists and its size. The state is dynamic, updated by each session and each public proposal.
stages.distribution: Discrete state (deal, no deal and talks, lockout) with long persistence; gap index changes in jumps at meetings and leaks.

stages.name: Stoppage duration hazard
stages.description: If no deal exists at expiry, the owners may lock out and stay out until costs rise. Hazard of agreement rises at deadlines: spring-training reporting, the scheduled opener, first missed paychecks. Reference classes (1990, 2021-22 and 1994-95 in baseball; NHL and NBA lockouts) show durations from days to a full season. The question is the cumulative probability that agreement lands before the date that permits play by May 31.
stages.distribution: Heavy-tailed duration with spikes at deadlines; right-censored; very small sample of comparable events.

stages.name: Ramp-up and first-game date
stages.description: After an agreement, players need a ramp-up period (spring training of about 3-4 weeks) and the league needs to publish a revised schedule. The first regular-season game therefore occurs at a lag after the deal that depends on the date and on whether the league shortens the preparation. Opening Day before May 31 requires the deal and ramp-up to fit before that date.
stages.distribution: Deterministic lag with small variance conditional on deal date; discontinuity at late dates where the league may cancel the season instead.

stages.name: Truncated-season go/no-go and games played
stages.description: If no deal exists late in the calendar, the parties decide whether to stage a minimum season for postseason and media revenue or cancel. The 600-game strike is about 40-46 days of league play, so doubleheaders and make-up dates are irrelevant to it; what matters is whether any season of at least about 40 games per team is staged. Mid-season stoppages matter only if they begin before roughly 600 games are complete.
stages.distribution: Trimodal: mass near the full 2,430 when a deal lands by spring, a smaller mode at 600-900 for a late truncated season, and a point mass at zero for cancellation.

stages.name: Settlement resolution and official count
stages.description: Opening Day resolves on whether the first 2027 regular-season game has taken place before May 31 and the games-played contract resolves on the count of MLB regular-season games above 600. Postponements, suspended games and tiebreakers are matters of official counting. Both depend on the contract text being read precisely.
stages.distribution: Binary on date; integer count near the schedule total; edge cases are rare.

stages.name: Non-agreement route: impasse, replacement players and injunction
stages.description: Owners may declare impasse and implement terms or schedule replacement-player games, and the union may file unfair-labour-practice charges; an NLRB complaint and federal injunction can restore prior terms and return players without a new agreement, as in March-April 1995. This route can start the season earlier than bargaining alone would, and it raises a counting question for both contracts if replacement-player games are played.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete states with long gaps between filings; a granted injunction gives a short fixed lag to play.

talent_strength.note: Team and player quality do not determine whether owners and the union reach a deal; the outcome is a league-wide bargaining process, not a contest between rosters.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent or matchup in a collective bargaining process; the closest analogue is the gap between the two sides' positions, covered under motivation and timeline inputs.

role_personnel.note: Who negotiates: commissioner, owners' committee, union leadership and membership votes.

availability_news.note: Reports of sessions, offers and lockout decisions with source reliability.

coaching_scheme.note: The bargaining strategy of each side (hardline versus incremental, public versus private) plays the role of tactics.

environment.note: Economic environment: revenue, television contracts and finance conditions that set each side's cost of waiting.

game_context_script.note: Expected path of the negotiation over the calendar, from expiry to the scheduled opener.

pace_volume.note: Games playable after a given start date; irrelevant at the 600 strike except to locate the late-start cutoff.

efficiency_conversion.note: No per-opportunity conversion rate exists; the outcome is a duration and a schedule count, so the nearest analogue is the hazard of agreement per week under the timeline input.

distribution_variance.note: Heavy-tailed duration and a trimodal games-played distribution (full, truncated, cancelled).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Deadlines, paychecks and stakes drive concessions.

officiating_rules.note: CBA and league rules on lockout, freeze and schedule revision; labour-law route of impasse, replacement players and injunction.

settlement_contract.note: Wording of before-date and above-threshold conditions; some edge cases unresolved.

mlb.cba_bargaining_positions.label: MLB-MLBPA bargaining positions: proposals on the economic system, salary-cap or floor demands, and public statements
mlb.cba_bargaining_positions.mechanism: Whether a deal is reached before expiry is set by the gap between owner and union proposals on the economic system and by each side's stated red lines.
mlb.cba_bargaining_positions.rationale: The sticking points in baseball talks are structural (revenue sharing, payroll limits, luxury-tax design, pre-arbitration pay) rather than incremental. A salary-cap demand by owners against a union that has historically refused any cap produces a hard gap that does not close by small concessions, so stated red lines matter more than the number of meetings.
mlb.cba_bargaining_positions.measurement: Code each public proposal or leak by topic (cap/floor, tax thresholds, revenue share, service-time, arbitration, draft, schedule length) as {proposed by, date, source tier}. Compute a gap index = number of topics with incompatible stated positions / topics open, updated at each bargaining session; add a red-line flag when either side calls an item a non-starter. As-of: public reports timestamped before the snapshot; discount single-source leaks to weight 0.5 until confirmed by a second outlet.
raw_data: dated list of proposals by topic and party
statements by commissioner and union leadership with timestamps
mlb.cba_bargaining_positions.why: Opening Day timing and games played are determined by whether the gap closes before or after the expiry and spring-training deadlines.

mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.label: Bargaining calendar hazard: days to expiry, owners' lockout decision date, spring-training and scheduled-opener deadlines
mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.mechanism: A deal can only arrive at certain points on a fixed calendar, and the hazard of agreement rises near binding deadlines.
mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.rationale: The CBA expiry on December 1, 2026 is the first deadline; the second is the February pitchers-and-catchers report date; the third is the scheduled opener. The market threshold date of May 31 and the 600-game strike value sit after all three, so the relevant question is the cumulative hazard through several deadlines, not at one.
mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.measurement: Build a discrete-time hazard on weekly steps from expiry to the scheduled opener plus 60 days: h(t) = P(agreement in week t | none yet), with features: weeks to the next hard deadline (spline), lockout in force flag, number of formal sessions in last 14 days, gap index. Fit on 1972, 1973, 1976, 1980-81, 1985, 1990, 1994-95, 2002, 2016 and 2021-22 episodes with strong shrinkage; map to P(first regular-season game before May 31) = P(agreement by the date implied by scheduled opening plus allowed ramp-up (about 3-4 weeks for spring training)). Dates taken from the published schedule and CBA text as of the snapshot.
free_sources: CBA text and prior CBA expiry timeline (free)
raw_data: calendar of deadlines: CBA expiry, report dates, scheduled opening day
historical stoppage episodes with start, end and cancelled games
mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.why: Converts a bargaining state into a probability that games start before a given date.

mlb.lockout_precedent_reference_class.label: Reference class of MLB and comparable league stoppages: duration, cancelled games and ramp-up needed before play
mlb.lockout_precedent_reference_class.mechanism: With very few comparable events the best prior for stoppage length is the historical distribution across baseball and other major leagues, adjusted for how much money is at stake.
mlb.lockout_precedent_reference_class.rationale: Only about nine baseball stoppages exist, ranging from a few days to a cancelled postseason, and 2021-22 delayed but did not shorten the schedule. Cross-sport lockouts (NHL 2004-05 lost the season, NBA 2011 lost about 16 games) add a heavy tail the baseball sample alone does not show.
mlb.lockout_precedent_reference_class.measurement: Table of MLB stoppages: type (strike or lockout), start, end, duration in days, regular-season games cancelled, spring training lost, ramp-up days between agreement and first game. Cross-sport table for NHL/NBA/NFL. Fit a mixture: P(short) from MLB (deal before first scheduled game), P(long) from pooled leagues; weight MLB episodes 1.0 and others 0.3; add a Beta prior (a=2, b=2) on P(any regular-season games cancelled). As-of: static history, update for any new episode.
free_sources: Wikipedia and league histories for NHL/NBA lockouts (free)
raw_data: episode table: dates, games lost, ramp-up days
mlb.lockout_precedent_reference_class.why: Gives the base rate for a stoppage reaching May 31 or removing three quarters of the schedule.

mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.label: Leverage state: owners' revenue and broadcast contract position versus players' strike-fund and salary exposure
mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.mechanism: A stoppage lasts as long as both sides' costs of waiting stay below their expected gain, which depends on revenue, television contracts, player earnings at risk and reserves.
mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.rationale: Regional sports network disruptions, national TV renewals and a rising luxury tax change who loses more from lost games. A lockout is a bet that players, who miss paychecks, concede first. Those costs are observable only through proxies, so the input must be built from revenue indicators and public finance data.
mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.measurement: Construct a leverage ratio = owners' cost of lost games per week (national media revenue share + gate + local media at risk, from public estimates and league-wide revenue reports) divided by players' cost per week (average salary share of the schedule, with a distribution weighting by arbitration and minimum-salary players) and a strike-fund and reserve indicator for the union. Update quarterly; treat as ordinal (-1, 0, +1) when exact data is missing. As-of: latest annual report or credible estimate before the snapshot.
free_sources: Forbes/Sportico franchise valuations and revenue estimates (free_limited)
MLBPA and league financial disclosures where public (free_limited)
raw_data: league and club revenue estimates
media contract terms
player payroll by tier
union reserves where disclosed
mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.why: Sets which side is under pressure to settle before games are lost.

mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.label: Schedule map from start date to games played: games per calendar day, scheduled finish date and make-up capacity
mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.mechanism: Games played in a shortened season equals scheduled games on dates after the first game, plus any games the league can add through doubleheaders and make-up days.
mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.rationale: Of the 2,430 scheduled games, the share that remain after a given delay depends on how the schedule is spread (about 13 to 15 games per calendar day on average, with fewer on Mondays and in April) and on whether MLB prefers to compress by doubleheaders, cancel series or play 162 by extending the season. The 600-game strike corresponds to a very late start or season cancellation.
mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.measurement: From the published schedule file (version at the snapshot) compute N(d) = league games scheduled on or after date d, and for each club the open dates in [d, last day]. Make-up capacity per club = min(open_dates_c(d) * q, 162 - games_scheduled_c(d)) with q = fraction of open dates converted to doubleheaders in recent make-up periods (estimate from 2021-2025 postponement make-ups, shrunk to 0.25 with k = 10 weeks). Predicted games G(d) = N(d) + (sum over 30 clubs of recoverable games)/2. Solve d* such that G(d*) = 600 games and also output the date after which fewer than 600 games remain. mlb.truncated_season_go_no_go.label: Go/no-go decision on staging a truncated season: minimum viable season length, postseason media revenue and pro-rated pay terms
mlb.truncated_season_go_no_go.mechanism: Fewer than 601 league games happens only if no season is staged or one starts in roughly mid-August or later; that is a joint owner-union decision to play a short season for postseason and TV revenue (2020) or to cancel (1994-95), not schedule arithmetic.
mlb.truncated_season_go_no_go.rationale: At 13-15 league games per day, 600 games is about 40-46 days of play, so make-up capacity never matters at this strike. The deciding question is whether, late in the calendar, the parties agree a minimum season: postseason national media money is large relative to a short regular season, which pushed the 2020 deal to a 60-game season (898 games played), while in 1994-95 the parties cancelled the postseason. Pay pro-rating and service-time credit decide whether players accept a short season.
mlb.truncated_season_go_no_go.measurement: Model P(season staged | no deal by date d) as a logistic in days remaining before the scheduled postseason start (minimum viable season assumed 40-60 team games, i.e. 600-900 league games, plus a 3-week ramp-up), an indicator that postseason media payments are contingent on games being played (from public contract reporting), and an indicator that a pro-rated pay and service-time framework is already agreed. Anchor with 2020 (staged, 60 games, agreement on terms imposed late June) and 1994-95 (postseason cancelled); prior P(staged | late deal) = 0.6 with Beta(3,2), updated on reports. Output P(games > 600) = P(deal or imposed season leaves >= 601 games).

mlb.impasse_replacement_legal_state.label: Impasse, implemented terms, replacement-player and labour-board/injunction state of the dispute
mlb.impasse_replacement_legal_state.mechanism: A stoppage can end without agreement: owners may declare bargaining impasse and implement terms or field replacement players, and the union may file unfair-labour-practice charges leading to an NLRB complaint and a federal injunction that restores prior terms and returns players.
mlb.impasse_replacement_legal_state.rationale: The 1994-95 strike ended when the NLRB obtained a federal injunction (March 31, 1995) restoring the expired terms, after owners had used replacement players in spring training. This route changes both timing and what counts: replacement-player games could be official regular-season games, and an injunction can start a season without a new CBA.
mlb.impasse_replacement_legal_state.measurement: Track as an ordinal state with dates: 0 bargaining, 1 lockout or strike, 2 impasse declared or terms implemented, 3 replacement players signed or scheduled, 4 ULP charge filed, 5 NLRB complaint or 10(j) petition, 6 injunction granted or denied. Hazard of season start = baseline from the bargaining hazard plus a state-specific term (state 6 granted implies return within about 3 weeks, from 1995). Sources timestamped; NLRB docket entries verified by case number. As-of: filings and announcements before the snapshot.

interactions.mechanism: The hazard of agreement in a given week is a baseline deadline hazard scaled by the gap size; the same deadline closes a small gap with high probability and a structural gap (such as a cap demand) with low probability, so the effect of a deadline depends on how wide the gap is.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit weekly hazard with gap index, deadline proximity and their product on stoppage episodes and test the product term, using the 2021-22 and 1990 cases as holdouts.

interactions.mechanism: When the remaining calendar drops below a minimum viable season, the outcome flips from 'play a short season' to 'cancel' depending on whether owners' postseason media revenue is at risk and players get pro-rated pay; above the threshold leverage matters little for the 600 strike.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast 2020 (staged with media money at stake) and 1994-95 (cancelled) and score the model on reported proposals by date; check that P(staged) is flat until the calendar threshold.

interactions.mechanism: The reference class is informative only if the leverage regime resembles the historical episode; when television revenue is guaranteed (owners' cost of waiting lower) long stoppages are more likely than the baseball sample implies.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition historical durations on a revenue-guarantee indicator across MLB, NHL and NBA episodes and compare tails.

interactions.mechanism: Once a lockout is declared the process moves from a pre-expiry regime where deals are common near the deadline to a lockout regime where only paycheck pressure and calendar deadlines close the gap, so new reports have different weights in each regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate separate hazards by regime flag and test whether news-dated shifts in agreement odds differ before and after the lockout start.

interactions.mechanism: Opening Day before May 31 needs agreement or an injunction at least a ramp-up period earlier; filing of an NLRB complaint adds a second hazard path whose timing is set by the court, not by deadlines, so the deal-date step can be bypassed.
interactions.how_to_test: Reconstruct 1995 (injunction March 31, games late April) and 2021-22 timelines and test whether a two-path hazard fits first-game dates better than a bargaining-only hazard.

nonlinearities.shape: spiking hazard near hard deadlines (expiry, report date, scheduled opener) and flat between
nonlinearities.why: Concessions concentrate when costs become real, so the probability of agreement is not smooth in time and a constant-hazard model misestimates both short and long stoppages.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold in days remaining: P(season staged) high until remaining calendar falls below a minimum viable season, then drops sharply
nonlinearities.why: Owners and players accept a short season only while it still carries a postseason and enough games to justify pro-rated pay, so the 600-game outcome is a step in the date of any deal.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold: little effect until a red-line item is declared, then a large drop in near-term agreement probability
nonlinearities.why: Structural disputes such as a salary cap do not close with small concessions, so the gap index matters mainly once it crosses a structural level.

catalog_entry.label: Playoff series winner, total games, spread and games hosted
catalog_entry.target: Winner, number of games, game margin of a best-of-N postseason series, or number of playoff games a club hosts.
catalog_entry.mechanism: A series is a first-to-N path through per-game win probabilities that differ by game: the bracket sets the home pattern, off days and rainouts move the rotation so each game has a different starter, bullpen fatigue accumulates (worse after extra innings, which have no automatic runner in the postseason) and resets, and rosters change between rounds. Winner, total games, spread and exact score are functions of the same series score; games hosted is seed probability times rounds reached times the home pattern, so before the bracket is set it is driven by regular-season seeding.

interactions.hypothesis: An ace on short rest or a bullpen game raises the next days' relief usage, so the rotation decision in game k conditions bullpen availability in k+1 and k+2; the effect on win probability is larger when off days are absent.

A favourite's per-game edge raises sweep probability convexly, and positive residual dependence fattens both the 4-0 and 4-3 cells, so spread and exact-score markets react to dependence much more than winner markets do.
Reliever concentration compresses the benefit of full-season depth; once the top three starters and top relievers account for most innings, adding depth beyond them does not raise win probability.

The probability of hosting 8 or more games is near zero for seeds 5-6 and depends on reaching the pennant round for bye seeds, so seed probability gates the hosting strike as a step rather than a smooth effect.

contract.settlement_definition: Seven live series, all with sampled rules text, all quoting World Series-style 'Championship Series' pairings (TB vs MIL 2026, TOR vs LAD 2025). KXMLBSERIES pays Yes if the named club wins the named series. KXMLBSERIESGAMES pays Yes if more than the strike (6.5) games are played; KXMLBSERIESGAMETOTAL pays Yes if the series has at least the strike (7) games, the same event expressed as greater_or_equal. KXMLBSERIESSPREAD pays Yes if the club wins by more than the strike in games (3.5, i.e. a 4-0 sweep in a best-of-seven). KXMLBSERIESEXACT and KXMLBSERIESSCORE pay Yes on one exact series record (e.g. 4-3 for the named club); they are the same contract under two tickers. KXMLBPLAYOFFHOST pays Yes if the club hosts at least the strike (8) playoff games over the whole postseason. No sampled text covers suspended or unfinished series, a relocated or neutral-site home game, or names a data source.

variants_and_edge_cases: Spread above 3.5 is only reachable in a best-of-seven (4-0); in a best-of-five the maximum margin is 3, so the same-form market would settle No structurally.

Total games: KXMLBSERIESGAMES (over 6.5, strike_type greater) and KXMLBSERIESGAMETOTAL (at least 7, greater_or_equal) are the same event in a best-of-seven; other rungs or shorter rounds need format-specific strikes.
Exact score: KXMLBSERIESEXACT and KXMLBSERIESSCORE each pay on one of eight cells (4-0..4-3 for either club); the cells sum to one, so the ladder is a full partition.

Hosting support by seed under the 12-team format: seeds 1-2 host 2-11 (DS games 1-2 are always at home; max DS 3 + LCS 4 + WS 4); seeds 3-4 host 2-13 (all of a best-of-3 Wild Card Series, then at most 2 in a DS as lower seed); seeds 5-6 host 0 in the Wild Card Series.

'Hosts' is not defined: a designated home game played at a temporary park (Athletics in Sacramento 2025-27), a borrowed park, or a neutral site after relocation could settle either way (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS).
Suspended games, rainouts or a series that does not finish are not addressed in any sampled rules text (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS).

Kalshi labels the World Series 'Championship Series' (ticker suffix WS, cross-league pairing); sampled markets are all World Series, so League Championship or Division Series variants are inferred, not seen.

mechanism.summary: A playoff series is a first-to-N path through per-game win probabilities that are not identical: the bracket fixes who hosts which game, each game has a different announced starter after off-day compression or a rainout, relievers accumulate fatigue (amplified by postseason extra innings without an automatic runner) and reset on off days, and rosters change between rounds. Winner, total games, game spread and exact score are functions of one final score (a margin above 3.5 games in a best-of-seven needs a 4-0 sweep), so the information inputs are the per-game probability vector and the dependence between games; the score distribution is output, not input. Playoff games hosted is the sum of designated home games over rounds reached; before the bracket exists it is driven by regular-season seed probabilities.

stages.name: Bracket, seeding and series format
stages.description: The 12-team bracket sets who plays whom: seeds 1-2 get byes, seeds 3-6 play a best-of-3 Wild Card Series hosted entirely by seeds 3-4, then best-of-5 and best-of-7 rounds with fixed home patterns. For hosting contracts priced before the season ends, seed probabilities from the remaining schedule and tiebreak rules are the dominant input; for single-series contracts this stage only fixes best-of-N and home pattern.
stages.distribution: Discrete bracket paths; deterministic format given seeds; path probabilities driven by upstream series results.

stages.name: Rosters, injuries and round-specific strength
stages.description: Each series has a submitted roster; injured players may return or be replaced between rounds, and key injuries during a series change strength. Team quality is therefore round-specific and uses a playoff-weighted rating (top starters, top relievers, regular lineup) rather than the full season average.
stages.distribution: Discrete roster states with continuous strength shifts; injury arrival roughly Poisson with heavy impact for stars.

stages.name: Starter assignment and rest under off days
stages.description: Postseason schedules have off days, so managers use three or four starters and may use an ace on short rest or a bullpen game. The identity of the starter in each game defines that game's win probability and the series is a sequence of different matchups rather than repeated draws of the same one. Rainouts and postponements move the off days, which changes rest and therefore which starter pitches each later game.
stages.distribution: Categorical starter per game with conditional dependence on prior games; bullpen-game tail.

stages.name: Per-game win probability and bullpen fatigue
stages.description: Given starters, lineups and park, a game is a win-probability draw with a small home edge. Short leashes make the bullpen cover a larger share of innings, and fatigue accumulates across consecutive games, resetting on off days. This couples games within a series: a heavy bullpen game two days ago lowers the next game's strength. Postseason extra innings use no automatic runner, so a long game can strip several relievers for the next one or two games.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per game with probability varying by game and weakly correlated across games through shared fatigue.

stages.name: Series dynamic program: winner, length, margin, exact score
stages.description: The series result is the first-to-N-wins path through the per-game probability vector, widened by any residual dependence between games. Winner, total games, margin (spread) and exact score are functions of one path; a sweep gives the largest margin and the shortest length. The state at the snapshot (games played, score, elimination) fixes the remaining tree. The score distribution is computed here as output; it is not an input.
stages.distribution: Discrete path distribution over scores 4-0 to 4-3 (or 3-0 to 3-2); lengths 4-7; correlated margins and lengths.

stages.name: Hosting count convolution and settlement
stages.description: For hosted-games contracts the count is the sum over rounds reached of designated home games in each series played, from the allocation table, seed and series length. Seeds 1-2 host 2-11 (DS games 1-2 are always theirs), seeds 3-4 host 2-13 because they host the whole Wild Card Series, seeds 5-6 host 0-10. Settlement uses official game counts; 'hosts' at a relocated or temporary park is undefined in the rules.
stages.distribution: Path-dependent integer sum; support 2-11 for bye seeds, 2-13 for seeds 3-4, 0-10 for seeds 5-6; lumpy, jumps by round.

mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.label: Playoff home-game allocation table: designated home team per game by round, seed and series length, with the as-played home log
mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.mechanism: Games hosted is a deterministic function of seed, rounds reached and series length through the format's home pattern; this input is that allocation rule plus the record of which club was the designated home team in each game already played.
mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.rationale: The path convolution itself is a model output; the information needed is the allocation rule. It is easy to get wrong: a best-of-3 Wild Card Series is hosted entirely by seeds 3-4, so they can reach 13 hosted games, while bye seeds reach at most 11 and seeds 5-6 host nothing in round one. Designated home team, not venue, must be logged because relocation is possible.
mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.measurement: Static table h(round, seed role, length): Wild Card Series best-of-3, higher seed (3 or 4) hosts every game (2 or 3), lower seed 0; Division Series 2-2-1, higher seed hosts G1, G2, G5 (2-3), lower seed G3, G4 (1-2); LCS 2-3-2 by seed and World Series 2-3-2 by regular-season record, higher seed hosts G1, G2, G6, G7 (2-4), lower seed G3-G5 (2-3). Combine with seed probabilities (mlb.season_sim, mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path) and series-length probabilities from the series model in the model layer, not here. As-of: format of the target season; per-game designated home team and venue logged after each game.

mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game.label: Projected starter for each game of the series after off days, with short-rest and bullpen-game probabilities
mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game.mechanism: Which starter pitches game k depends on the announced rotation, off days, ace usage on short rest and the chance of a bullpen game.
mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game.rationale: In a short series the top starters pitch more games, so team strength is not constant across games. Game 5 of a division series or Game 7 may feature an ace on short rest or an opener. Postseason off days compress the rotation to three or four men, making the per-game win probability a sequence rather than a single number.
mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game.measurement: For each remaining game build a probability table P(starter = s) from rotation order, days of rest (off days count), number of starts so far, manager history of three- versus four-man rotations (postseason 2015-2025), injuries, and statements by managers (weight 0.5 until announced). Convert to per-game win probability by log5 with starter quality (SIERA/Stuff+ blended with 3-year projection, shrinkage k = 60 IP) plus bullpen-day penalty for P(opener). As-of: announcements through the snapshot time; probables update with each game. Postponements: a rainout shifts every later game by a day and adds rest, so recompute rest days and starter eligibility after any postponement in the official schedule.

pitcher days of rest, innings and pitch counts in series

mlb.series_bullpen_cumulative_workload.label: Cumulative bullpen workload across the series: relievers' pitches on consecutive days and off-day resets
mlb.series_bullpen_cumulative_workload.mechanism: High-leverage relievers cannot pitch every day, so fatigue and unavailability accumulate over games and reset on off days.
mlb.series_bullpen_cumulative_workload.rationale: In a short series managers use the best relievers heavily, which makes the closer's availability in game 5 depend on usage in games 3 and 4 and on the schedule of off days. This is a dynamic availability state, unlike the regular-season rest rules, and it can reduce a stronger team's edge late in the series.
mlb.series_bullpen_cumulative_workload.measurement: Track reliever pitches in the last 1, 2 and 3 days from play-by-play; flag unavailability when pitches >= 25 yesterday or 3 consecutive days (thresholds from regular-season 2021-25 usage, calibrated per manager, shrunk k = 30 appearances). Compute team leverage-weighted bullpen availability score = sum over relievers of (talent x P(available)), as of the lineup-card time. Reset on off days using the observed usage patterns in postseason series. Postseason extra innings use no automatic runner, so log extra-inning length per game; a 12+ inning game removes several relievers for one to two days and is the main source of multi-game depletion.
raw_data: reliever pitch counts by date, leverage index of entries, off-day calendar
mlb.series_bullpen_cumulative_workload.why: Series total games and winner depend on late-series bullpen state that regular-season averages miss.

mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.label: Postseason roster eligibility between rounds: injured-player replacement, roster resets and who can be on the series roster
mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.mechanism: Each series has its own submitted roster, so an injured player may return or be replaced between rounds, which changes team strength round by round.
mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.rationale: A team's strength entering the league championship series is not the same roster as in the division series; hitters and pitchers can be swapped between rounds under league rules. This matters for hosting-count markets that span several rounds and for any series where injuries occur in the previous round.
mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.measurement: For each team and round: Delta = sum over players added of projected rest-of-season WAR per 150 games (ZiPS/Steamer average) times expected playing-time share, minus the same for players removed from the prior-round roster; unconfirmed injured players enter with probability p = P(activated by deadline) from mlb.rehab_progression_stage rather than as a flag. Convert Delta to runs per game (wins/10). Log submitted rosters by round 2012-2025 from MLB transactions to estimate the base rate of injured-list replacements per round. Units: runs per game. As-of: roster submission deadline and public injury reports available at the snapshot.

mlb.series_per_game_win_prob_vector.label: Market-free per-game win probability for each remaining game of a series, built from starters, bullpen availability, lineup and home edge
mlb.series_per_game_win_prob_vector.mechanism: The series is a first-to-N path through game probabilities that differ by game because the starter, bullpen state and home team change; this input is the vector p_1..p_N those components produce.
mlb.series_per_game_win_prob_vector.rationale: This replaces the series length and exact-score distributions as the true information input: those are deterministic transforms of this vector plus within-series dependence. Building it from components (not from series or game prices, which are benchmarks only) is what allows it to move when a rotation is announced or a closer is unavailable.
mlb.series_per_game_win_prob_vector.measurement: For game k: logit p_k = a0 + b1 x D_team + b2 x D_sp x s_k + b3 x D_pen x (1 - s_k) + b4 x D_lineup + h_park, where D_team is postseason-weighted team rating difference in runs per game, D_sp is probable-starter projected RA9 difference weighted by expected starter innings share s_k (about 0.55), D_pen the availability-weighted bullpen rating difference, D_lineup the lineup-versus-hand wRC+ difference, and h_park the park-specific home term shrunk toward +0.035 (k = 300 games). Starter identity is a mixture over mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game. Coefficients fitted on 2012-2025 postseason and late-season games with ridge shrinkage. The calculation uses only projections, rosters and park data; no quoted odds enter. As-of: probables and availability at the snapshot.

mlb.series_game_dependence.label: Within-series dependence of game outcomes beyond the modelled starter and fatigue effects (residual correlation parameter)
mlb.series_game_dependence.mechanism: If game results share an unmodelled common factor (injury carried through the series, a mis-rated team), the series score distribution is wider than the independent-games path implies: more sweeps and more seventh games.
mlb.series_game_dependence.rationale: Spread (sweep) and exact-score cells are tail cells of the score distribution, so a small positive correlation shifts them far more than it shifts the winner probability. The parameter must be estimated, not assumed zero, and its uncertainty carried.
mlb.series_game_dependence.measurement: Fit a game-level logistic model on 1995-2025 postseason games using pregame component predictions as offset; add a series-level random effect and estimate its standard deviation by marginal likelihood; convert to an equivalent pairwise correlation rho with a bootstrap interval over series. Compare predicted versus observed frequency of 4-0 and 4-3 results by best-of-N format. As-of: static history, refit each offseason.

mlb.series_game_dependence.why: Sweep-only spread contracts and exact-score cells depend on tail shape, which is set by this dependence.

interactions.mechanism: An ace on short rest or a bullpen game raises the next days' relief usage, so the rotation decision in game k conditions bullpen availability in k+1 and k+2; the effect on win probability is larger when off days are absent.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress next-game bullpen availability on prior starter innings and rest, then compare win probability residuals in postseason games after bullpen days.

interactions.mechanism: Residual dependence between games widens the score distribution for a given per-game edge: sweeps and seventh games both become more likely while the winner probability barely moves, so spread and exact-score cells respond to dependence and winner markets do not.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare observed 4-0 and 4-3 frequencies (1995-2025) against simulations from fitted per-game vectors with rho = 0 versus the estimated rho, stratified by per-game edge.

interactions.mechanism: Reliever concentration compresses the benefit of full-season depth; once the top three starters and top relievers account for most innings, adding depth beyond them does not raise win probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare rating variants (full roster versus top-heavy weighting) in predicting playoff game outcomes across 2012-2025.

interactions.mechanism: Seed fixes which hosting totals are reachable: 8+ needs at least the pennant round for a bye seed, is easier for seed 3-4 through three Wild Card home games, and is nearly impossible for seed 5-6, so seed probability enters the hosting strike as a gate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(hosts >= k) conditional on final seed and rounds reached across 2022-2025 brackets and compare with a model that uses series win probability without seed.

interactions.mechanism: Under elimination the trailing manager shortens starters' leash and uses top relievers early, so win probability behaves differently in elimination games than in game one of a series.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact elimination flag with starter innings share and test whether game win probability residuals differ for elimination versus non-elimination games.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in the per-game edge: sweep probability rises faster than linearly as the favourite strengthens
nonlinearities.why: Series outcome is a binomial-type path function, so a small per-game edge becomes a larger series edge and sweep-only spread and exact-score cells change nonlinearly.

nonlinearities.shape: step changes in win probability by starter identity, with a tail for bullpen games
nonlinearities.why: The best starter pitches a game with a clearly higher win probability, and a bullpen game lowers it, so per-game strength is multimodal across games.

nonlinearities.shape: step function in rounds reached; integer-valued sum with a jump at each round
nonlinearities.why: Home games are added in blocks by round, so the count is a lumpy function of advancement rather than a smooth variable.
